title: Acceptance checklist for tool invocation schemas, streaming JSON, and graceful error modes
creator: Asha Patel
description: Context: Customers rely on consistent structured output (JSON) and function/tool invocation semantics for downstream automation. Recent upgrades to streaming and schema enforcement require explicit acceptance criteria to avoid regressions for existing SDKs and integrations. Goal: Define pass/fail conditions for shaping structured output, tool call payloads, streaming chunk behavior, and error/fallback modes. This ticket captures requirements, sample schemas, and validation tests for runtime and console teams to implement and verify. Scope: - Enforce canonical tool-call envelope for all models behind Redwood API. - Streaming: ensure JSON object(s) are emit-safe for incremental parsers with explicit chunk types. - Error modes: define fallback behaviors when model output is malformed, partial, or violates schema. - Observability hooks: metrics and logs for parse errors and fallbacks. Out of scope: - Changes to model training or sampling behavior. - Language-specific SDKs beyond standard JSON contract and HTTP semantics.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Tool invocation envelope: every tool call must be wrapped with top-level fields {"tool_name": string, "version": string, "args": object|string, "metadata": object?}. Requests and responses must validate against the published OpenAPI-style schema without additional top-level keys.

AC-2: Structured output schema conformance: For endpoints that declare a schema, 99.9% of successful responses in a 24-hour production window must validate against the declared JSON Schema for the model+route combination. Any schema validation failures must trigger a regression alert.

AC-3: Streaming chunk specification: When streaming structured output, the runtime must emit annotated chunk types: 'prefix' (optional), 'json_chunk' (escaped/serialized fragment), 'final' (complete JSON object), and 'error' (structured error message). Chunks must include monotonic sequence IDs for reassembly.

AC-4: Incremental parse safety: Clients performing streaming incremental parse (no buffering of entire response) must be able to reconstruct the final JSON without requiring application-layer heuristics beyond concatenation of 'json_chunk' fragments in sequence order.

AC-5: Malformed output handling: If the model produces non-JSON or schema-violating JSON: - The runtime must attempt two automated recoveries: a) apply deterministic JSON reassembly heuristics (bracket balancing, truncated-string repair) and b) re-run with a stricter decoding mode (same prompt + system flag). - If both recoveries fail, the runtime must emit an 'error' chunk with parse diagnostics and a fallback plain-text payload, and mark the request as 'parsed_with_fallback' in tracing.

AC-6: Tool call idempotency and retry semantics: Tool invocation requests originating from streaming outputs must include a stable call_id. The runtime will deduplicate invocations for the same call_id across up to 3 retries; after 3 retries a non-destructive 'duplicate_call' flag must be sent to the tool consumer.

AC-7: Backwards compatibility: Default behavior for clients not opting into schema enforcement must remain unchanged. New strict-mode contract is opt-in via header 'X-Redwood-Output-Mode: strict' or route config. Opt-in users must receive schema validation errors explicitly and by default block invalid outputs from returning a successful 200 response.

AC-8: Observability: Expose metrics: structured_output.validation_failures.count, streaming.chunk_drop.count, tool_call.duplicate.count, tool_call.latency.p50/p95, and error_recovery.success.count. Dashboards for these metrics must be available in Console release runtime-2.4.

AC-9: Acceptance tests: Automated suite must include unit tests, integration tests (runtime + model), and a synthetic end-to-end test that simulates partial stream drops and validates client reassembly correctness. All tests must pass in the CI gate before merging the runtime change.

AC-10: Documentation + SDK: Public docs must include exact JSON Schema examples, sample streaming reassembly pseudocode, and explicit guidance on error codes and retry semantics. Example must be present in the PR for docs changes and reviewed by Developer Experience.

AC-11: Rollout safety: New strict-mode behavior must be feature-flagged and ramped to 5%/25%/100% traffic over 2 weeks with automated rollback criteria if validation_failures.count > 0.1% at 5% ramp or >0.05% at 25% ramp.
test_plan: TP-1: Unit tests for schema validator: feed 50+ variant payloads including extra keys, missing required fields, type mismatches — expect exact failure codes.
TP-2: Streaming parser simulations: synthetic generator emits well-formed, truncated, and interleaved chunk orders. Verify reassembly with sequence IDs in-order and out-of-order recovery behavior.
TP-3: Fault injection: runtime returns intentionally corrupted JSON mid-stream. Verify recovery heuristics path a) and b) execute, 'error' chunk emitted, and trace contains 'parsed_with_fallback'.

TP-4: Tool invocation dedupe test: simulate three identical call_id invocations with network retry; confirm the tool consumer receives only one effective invocation and receives duplicate_call metadata on later attempts.
TP-5: Backcompat smoke: run legacy clients against non-strict routes to confirm no change in 200 behaviors and that SDKs are unaffected.
TP-6: Load test: 10k streaming requests/hour with mixed structured output and tool-calls to surface latency regressions; baseline p95 must not regress by more than 10%.
TP-7: Monitoring alert test: intentionally trigger schema validation failures and confirm alert rules fire and PagerDuty runbook is executed.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag behind 'structured-output-strict' default off. Canary with engineering and select partner accounts only.
Phase 1: Enable strict-mode for 5% of traffic for 72 hours; monitor metrics and logs; run automated rollback checks.
Phase 2: Ramp to 25% for 4 days if metrics healthy; gather feedback from SDK teams and developer partners.
Phase 3: Full enablement for paying customers only; keep legacy behavior for free-tier clients for one additional week.
Phase 4: Complete rollout to 100% and update public docs; deprecate old 'lenient' console toggle after 90 days if no major issues.
success_metrics: S1: Schema validation failure rate for strict-mode routes <= 0.01% over first 30 days post-rollout.
S2: Streaming reassembly success rate >= 99.99% in synthetic end-to-end tests.
S3: No more than 0.02% increase in p95 latency for streaming endpoints compared to pre-rollout baseline.
S4: Tool call duplicate invocations observed by tools < 0.001% after dedupe implementation.
notes: Sample tool-call envelope example: {"tool_name":"web_search","version":"v1","args":{"query":"latest redwood runtime benchmarks"},"metadata":{"origin":"assistant"}}
Error chunk example: {"type":"error", "sequence":4, "code":"PARSE_FAILURE", "message":"Unexpected token at offset 142", "recovery_attempts": ["repair_brackets", "strict_redecode"]}
Observability: include structured logs with fields: route, model, call_id, sequence, schema_id, validation_result, recovery_path. Ensure logs are parsable and ingested to the metrics pipeline.
Related docs/prs: link to ENG-20448 runtime chunking proposal (referenced in dependencies).
